request.title: Autumn campaign: demand far above plan
request.instructions: Our autumn campaign (Herbstzauber) works almost too well: order intake is far above plan and several new sales orders have no production order yet. Make sure we can deliver what we sold without burning out the factories. Decide whether the campaign has to be throttled (do not stop it completely, we still want the sales), ask Cora to plan the new orders, Max to secure capacity, and Lara to secure the material.

# Planning autumn bundles can still end late

Rule: A healthy-looking factory queue and material projection do not guarantee that a large unplanned autumn bundle will finish on time; verify the post-change late-order KPI and material-shortage projection before treating the plan as sufficient.

Applies when: Several confirmed but unplanned sales orders are added together during a campaign spike and no extra capacity lever is booked.

tasks.plan:
# Goal
Secure the smallest effective production-capacity package after Cora's replanning of `SO-2301`..`SO-2308`. The live bottleneck is still the `FOAM-HR35` shortage from `2026-11-12`, so this step should only book capacity that is actually needed and keep the package as small as possible.

# Inputs
- Live ERP overview: `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=8`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `costOfMeasuresEur=0`.
- Live capacity: both `F-NORTH` and `F-SOUTH` currently run at `40 sofas/day` for the next 10 workdays with `2/2 regular workers`.
- Live material projection for `FOAM-HR35`: `usableNow=6000`, no open purchase orders, first shortage `production is held back from 2026-11-12`.
- Simulations already run:
  - `request_overtime` on `F-NORTH` from `2026-10-05` to `2026-10-16`: cost `EUR 14,000`, no KPI improvement, shortage only moves to `2026-11-11`.
  - `request_overtime` on `F-SOUTH` from `2026-10-05` to `2026-10-16`: cost `EUR 14,000`, no KPI improvement, shortage only moves to `2026-11-10`.
  - Combined overtime in both factories: cost `EUR 28,000`, still no KPI improvement, and it introduces a new `BEAM-PINE-80` shortage from `2026-10-30`.
  - `request_temp_workers` for 1 worker in `F-NORTH` from `2026-10-05` to `2026-10-16`: the agency start shifts to `2026-10-08`, cost `EUR 1,820`, shortage moves to `2026-11-11`.
  - `request_temp_workers` for 1 worker in `F-SOUTH` from `2026-10-05` to `2026-10-16`: the agency start shifts to `2026-10-08`, cost `EUR 1,820`, shortage moves to `2026-11-11`.
- Wiki: `company/overview.md` (default priority 5, customer lag convention), `protocols/handoffs.md` (Max request needs factory, date range, shortfall, budget), `protocols/ordered-delegation.md` (ordered follow-ups if needed), `rules/capacity-levers.md` (simulate combinations first; temp workers before overtime), `rules/customer-notices.md` (not needed here), `wiki/log.md` (past capacity decisions and lessons).

# Steps
1. Book `1` temporary worker in `F-SOUTH` for `2026-10-08` through `2026-10-16` with `erp__request_temp_workers`. This is the smallest simulated package that adds capacity without the extra cost and side effects of overtime.
2. Verify the live ERP overview and factory capacity after the booking. Record the booked measure, its cost, and the resulting daily capacity in `F-SOUTH` versus `F-NORTH`.
3. If the live result differs from the simulation, capture the exact ERP result and report the actual capacity package and KPI state without adding any extra measure.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-a2a-56d0b370-df4f-431d-af1c-4ff1a00c786e.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-a2a-56d0b370-df4f-431d-af1c-4ff1a00c786e_plan_1.md`

# Risks and open questions
- A capacity booking alone does not clear the current lateness KPI because the dominant limiter is still `FOAM-HR35`.
- `F-NORTH` and `F-SOUTH` were equivalent in the single-worker simulations, so the chosen factory is a tie-breaker, not a modeled necessity.
- Approver must confirm that the smallest effective package is acceptable even though it does not reduce `lateOrders` immediately.

# Goal

Report the ERP-computed completion and delivery dates for each order after execution, plus any orders still late and whether the replan creates a real capacity gap or material shortage that needs follow-up.

# Inputs
- ERP overview now: `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8`, `materialShortages={}`.
- The 8 unplanned orders total `970` sofas and are `SO-2301`..`SO-2308`.
- CRM order facts: `SO-2303` and `SO-2304` are tier A; the others are tier B. Promised delivery dates run from `2026-10-26` (`SO-2301`) through `2026-11-24` (`SO-2308`).
- Capacity check: both factories show `40 sofas/day` for each of the next 10 workdays; all machines are running and each factory has 2 regular workers.
- Queue check: both factory queues are currently empty, so there is no existing production priority to disturb.
- Material checks: `BEAM-PINE-80`, `FAB-OAT-01`, `FAB-ANTH-02`, and `FOAM-HR35` all show no shortage within 70 workdays.

# Goal
Keep Herbstzauber selling, but prevent the 8 unplanned autumn orders from turning into factory overload or late customer promises. Right now the problem is 8 confirmed unplanned sales orders totaling 970 sofas, with KPI still clean: 0 late orders, 0 late sofas, 0 orders late without customer notice, and 0 shortages.

# Inputs
- ERP overview on 2026-10-05: 26 sales orders, 18 planned production orders, 8 unplanned orders (`SO-2301`..`SO-2308`), and KPI still at zero for lateness and shortages.
- CRM demand trend: plan baseline 1800 sofas, confirmed unplanned demand 970 sofas, intake 54% above plan, Herbstzauber active at 100% daily budget until 2026-10-31.
- Unplanned orders are `SO-2301`..`SO-2308`; tier-A customers among them are `SO-2303` (C-04) and `SO-2304` (C-02).
- Factory capacity is 40 sofas/day at both `F-NORTH` and `F-SOUTH` for the next 15 workdays, with no late production orders today.
- Material projections show no shortage within 70 workdays for `BEAM-PINE-80`, `FAB-OAT-01`, or `FAB-ANTH-02`.
- Wiki read: `index.md`, `protocols/handoffs.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, `rules/capacity-levers.md`, `rules/customer-notices.md`, `protocols/release-checklist.md`, `log.md`.
- Company wiki: `index.md`, `protocols/handoffs.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, `rules/capacity-levers.md`, `rules/customer-notices.md`, `protocols/release-checklist.md`; key rule is to compare material first, then capacity, and only tell customers about orders that are late in ERP.
- What-if results: adding overtime for `F-NORTH` alone or `F-SOUTH` alone is feasible, but the read-only simulator returned `workdays: 0` and no KPI change because it does not model the live production lever impact for this change.
- What-if results: temporary-worker simulation could not be used meaningfully because the simulator rejected the arguments (`count must be 1-4`), so capacity sizing still needs live execution checks.

# Steps
1. Throttle Herbstzauber in CRM, but do not stop it: set campaign `CMP-HERBST` to `dailyBudgetPct: 50` so at least half of the daily budget keeps running, keep status `active`, and record the reason that intake is 54% above plan and should be slowed while the current backlog is worked through.
2. Ask Cora to plan the 8 unplanned sales orders `SO-2301`..`SO-2308` into production orders, keeping tier-A orders protected first and preserving existing priorities. Request her to return the ERP expected completion/delivery dates and any orders that are still late after replanning.
3. Ask Max to secure extra production capacity only if needed after Cora’s replan, using the smallest effective package of overtime and temporary workers for `F-NORTH` and/or `F-SOUTH`; the request must include the factory, date range, and the shortage in sofas per day or total sofas.
4. Ask Lara to secure material only if Cora’s replan reveals a real shortage for the 8 orders. The request must name the relevant SKU(s), quantity, and needed-by date, and it should rely on the current material projections showing no shortage within 70 workdays unless the replan changes that.
5. Recheck the ERP KPI after the planning/capacity actions. If any order becomes late, then use `crm__list_orders(riskOnly=true)` and, for each order that is late in ERP, record the new ERP delivery date and send a short customer notice, starting with tier-A customers and only naming dates that ERP shows.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-01M61GB8K1C4SJN0Q56A3083MC.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-01M61GB8K1C4SJN0Q56A3083MC_plan_1.md`

# Risks and open questions
- The live CRM campaign change still needs execute-time confirmation because the read-only simulator did not support `update_campaign`, so the exact throttle decision cannot be validated there.
- The current KPI is clean, so the main risk is creating avoidable cost or over-throttling demand while the factories still have normal visible capacity.
- We need the live replan result before deciding whether Max or Lara actually need to act; no customer notice should be sent unless ERP shows a late expected delivery date.
- The 8 unplanned orders are the only demand spike in scope right now, but they are large enough that a live replan could still create a bottleneck not visible in the current projections.

# Goal
Secure the real material shortage exposed by Cora’s replanned SO-2301..SO-2308 production plan. The live ERP shows a `FOAM-HR35` shortage holding production back from `2026-11-12`; no other current material shortage is confirmed in the live projection.

- Live ERP overview: `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=8`, `costOfMeasuresEur=0`, and `FOAM-HR35` is the only material shortage shown.
- Live material projection for `FOAM-HR35`: `usableNow=6000`, first shortage at `2026-11-12`, no open purchase orders.
- Live material projection for `BEAM-PINE-80`: no shortage within 70 workdays, with open POs already covering it.
- Supplier facts from the wiki and ERP: `S-FOAMTEC` is the only supplier for `FOAM-HR35`, lead time `5` workdays, unit price `9.5 EUR`, minimum order `500`, maximum `20000`, no express option.
- Wiki: `index.md` (company wiki rules), `protocols/handoffs.md` (procurement request needs SKU, quantity, needed-by date, reason, current KPI; returns PO ids, quantities, supplier, arrival dates, cost, KPI after), `protocols/ordered-delegation.md` (dependent work must be chained in order), `suppliers/overview.md` (FOAM-HR35 supplier rule), `entities/s-foamtec.md` (supplier facts).

# Steps
1. Create one purchase order for `FOAM-HR35` with `supplierId=S-FOAMTEC`, `quantity=1330`, and the note `Cover FOAM-HR35 shortage caused by the replanned SO-2301..SO-2308 production plan`.
2. Verify the ERP result, including the purchase order id, ETA, and total cost, and then re-check the material projection for `FOAM-HR35` if needed to confirm the shortage is cleared in the live state.
3. Report the purchase order id, quantity, supplier, arrival date, cost, and the KPI after execution.
